Bereshit Rabbah 92:3

F — OUR 43:14 READ TWICE, and both readings recorded: (a) the plain — "the man" is the Egyptian ruler, "your other brother" is Simeon, "and Benjamin" is himself, "as I am bereaved" of Joseph and of Simeon; (b) R. Yashya ben Levi's exile reading — "the man" is the Holy One (Exodus 15:3, "the LORD is a man of war"), "your other brother" the TEN TRIBES, "and Benjamin" the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, "as I am bereaved, I am bereaved" the first and second destructions, closing "I shall not be bereaved again" [the verse carried as both a father's prayer and a national petition — dual-track]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:1

F — [anchored at OUR 43:9, which it quotes twice; its home verse is 44:18 in gen_67's span] Judah's pledge read through Proverbs 6:1-3 ("if you became SURETY ‹עָרַב› for your friend… you are snared by the words of your mouth… do this and be delivered") — the surety, the handshake, and the snare each matched to a clause of OUR 43:9, and the deliverance read as going to cleave to the dust of the man's feet; carried with it R. Ḥanina's SIX-ITEM PRACTICAL LIST — flee from three (accepting deposits, counselling a girl's refusal of her betrothal, standing surety between two parties) and cleave to three (the levirate release, the nullification of vows, and making peace) — with the wordplay that a deposit ‹פִּקָּדוֹן› ("pikadon") should be heard as "take it out ‹פּוּק דּוֹן›" [a law-shaped list mounted on this block's own suretyship; the register's testing shelf will meet these again]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:2

F — "behold, the kings convened, they passed together" (Psalms 48:5) read as JUDAH AND JOSEPH, and "passed ‹עָבְרוּ›" heard as "filled with FURY ‹עֶבְרָה›" — each king enraged at the other, while "they saw and were astonished" is OUR 43:33 ("the men looked at one another in astonishment"): the tribes stood out of it saying kings contend with kings, what is that to us [the confrontation of gen_67 already sited in this block's banquet — the astonishment at the seating is the chain's proof the duel had begun]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:3

F — [anchored at OUR 43:28; home verses Genesis 50:1-2, gen_73's span] WHY JOSEPH DIED BEFORE HIS BROTHERS, two answers: Rabbi says because he embalmed his father (God: "could I not preserve my righteous one?"); the Rabbis say Jacob himself commanded it, and the cause is instead that ALMOST FIVE TIMES Judah said "your servant my father" in Joseph's hearing and Joseph kept silent — the count running from OUR 43:28 through 44:24, 27, 30, 31 [an ink count with a lethal consequence attached, spanning this block and the next; the honor owed a father measured by silences]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:20

F — [anchored at OUR 43:34; home verses Genesis 49:24-26, gen_72's span] R. Levi's TWENTY-TWO-YEAR ABSTINENCE: through all the years he did not see his brothers Joseph tasted no wine, and they tasted none until they saw him — proven from OUR 43:34's "they drank and became drunk WITH HIM" (with him they drank; without him they did not) [the numeric rider credited 92:5 also carries, read here at its own seat]; the section's remaining dossier — the bow read as passion drawn and slackened, the father's (or mother's) image cooling his blood, Joseph as one set apart ‹נָזִיר› ("nazir") because his brothers separated him — belongs to gen_72 and is recorded there when read

gen_67_cup_and_surety.t: The cup and the surety: Judah's speech (44:1-34)
mat: Bereshit Rabbah 92:7

F — THE TEN A-FORTIORI ARGUMENTS OF SCRIPTURE, and OUR 44:8 IS THE CENSUS'S FIRST MEMBER: R. Yishmael teaches that ten inferences of the light-and-heavy form ‹קַל וָחֹמֶר› ("kal va-ḥomer" — middah I1) are written in Scripture, opening with "behold, the silver we found we returned to you — how then should we steal?" and continuing through Moses' "the children of Israel did not heed me, how then will Pharaoh?" (Exodus 6:12), the father's spittle and seven days against the Presence's fourteen (Numbers 12:14), "while I yet live you are defiant — how much more after my death" (Deuteronomy 31:27), the footmen-and-horses and peaceful-land-and-Jordan pair (Jeremiah 12:5), "here in Judah we are afraid, how much more at Ke'ila" (I Samuel 23:3), the righteous requited on earth (Proverbs 11:31), Shushan's five hundred against the provinces (Esther 9:12), and the whole vine unusable against the charred (Ezekiel 15:5) [a MIDDOT-layer exhibit of the first order: this unit's verse is the tradition's own type-specimen for the inference rule the machine cites everywhere — logic/MIDDOT.md seat]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:3

F — "like golden apples in silver settings ‹מַשְׂכִּיּוֹת› is a word spoken ‹עַל אָפְנָיו› ("al ofnav")" (Proverbs 25:11) applied to Judah's approach: as a WHEEL ‹אוֹפָן› ("ofan") shows its face on every side, his words were found sound by every party at once [the persuasion measured by universality, not force]; and the passage cites AKILAS THE PROSELYTE's rival rendering of the verse by name — a translator quoted inside the midrash [the two-shelves seam again: the chain naming and weighing a translation beside Onkelos, as at the 25:3 seam of gen_39]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:4

F — "counsel in a man's heart is deep water, and a man of understanding draws it out" (Proverbs 20:5) as the DEEP-WELL MODEL: the well whose water was cold and good but unreachable until someone tied rope to rope, thread to thread and cord to cord and drew — so Judah answered Joseph on every single matter, not relenting, until he reached his heart [the speech modelled as an incremental extraction, each clause a knot; the mechanism behind row 2's universality]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:7

F — the confrontation's PHYSICAL DOSSIER on OUR 44:17-18, framed by "wisdom fortifies the wise more than ten rulers in a city" (Ecclesiastes 7:19) read of Joseph: Judah's roar carrying four hundred parsangs until Ḥushim son of Dan leapt from Canaan to join it, both lions roaring (Job 4:10 — the same verse gen_64 row 14 spent on Simeon's scream) until Egypt was near upended and the teeth of Joseph's warriors fell out; the brothers kicking the ground into furrows; the SIGNS of Judah's rage disputed (blood from both eyes / the single hair over his heart that tore through five garments of armor); Joseph kicking the stone pillar he sat on into a heap of pebbles; and Judah's sword that would not leave its scabbard — "this one must be a God-fearing man" [the duel as a test of strength that ends in recognition of fear-of-Heaven, not in force]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:9

F — R. Ḥiyya bar Abba: everything Judah says from OUR 44:18 until "Joseph could not restrain himself" (45:1, gen_68's span) is CONCILIATION THREE WAYS AT ONCE — toward Joseph (see how he gives his life for Rachel's son, the very brother he once sold), toward the brothers (see how he gives his life for a brother), and toward Benjamin ("as I give my life for you, so would I for your brother") [one speech discharging three separate estrangements — the repentance the sale of gen_60 has been waiting on]; and a recorded dispute on what follows: R. Ḥama bar Ḥanina holds Joseph did NOT act properly in clearing the room, since one kick would have killed him, against R. Shmuel bar Naḥman — he acted properly, knowing his brothers were not suspected of bloodshed [dual-track; the risk assessment carried both ways into gen_68]

This unit spans the WHOLE of chapter 44, so the reading carries Vayigash's opening seventeen verses (Judah's speech, 44:18-34) under the block-boundary law that put 32:1-3 inside gen_55. HEADLINES: THE TEN A-FORTIORI ARGUMENTS OF SCRIPTURE, and 44:8 is the census's FIRST MEMBER — this unit's verse is the tradition's own type-specimen for the light-and-heavy inference the machine cites everywhere; Judah's speech as CONCILIATION THREE WAYS at once (toward Joseph, the brothers, and Benjamin), the repentance the sale of gen_60 was waiting on, with the recorded dispute over whether Joseph's clearing of the room was reckless; the deep-well model of persuasion (rope tied to rope until he reached the heart); the wheel that shows its face on every side, with AKILAS THE PROSELYTE cited by name beside Onkelos — the two-shelves seam; the duel's physical dossier ending in "this one must be a God-fearing man"; Judah's three crowning speeches completed on the record. Onkelos: DIVINATION CONVERTED TO INVESTIGATION at both seats — the righteous one does not practice augury; the finding of iniquity made passive and set "from before the LORD"; and "torn, torn" rendered "surely killed" in exact agreement with gen_60's reading seven chapters back. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

mat: Bereshit Rabbah 93:10

F — THE REBUKE AS A JUDGMENT-DAY A-FORTIORI (Abba Kohen Bardela): if Joseph, the youngest of the tribes, rebuked his brothers and they could not answer him (OUR 45:3), and if Balaam the gentile sage could not withstand the rebuke of his own donkey, how much more when the Holy One rebukes each person according to his station (Psalms 50:21) [the block's central verse read as a model of judgment — argues the light-and-heavy form, and note that gen_67 row 1 seated that very inference rule's census]; "come near to me, and they came near" — HE SHOWED THEM THE CIRCUMCISION as the proof of identity [the body as evidence]; the three titles of OUR 45:8 parsed as a patron to the king, a lord of the house, and a ruler of the land; and "my MOUTH is speaking to you" (45:12) read as IN THE HOLY TONGUE — the language itself the credential
Bereshit Rabbah 93:11

F — R. Elazar ben Azarya's independent statement of the same a-fortiori, and the sharper form: Joseph was FLESH AND BLOOD, and they could not stand; the Holy One is judge, litigant and bench at once, so no flesh and blood will stand before Him [carried as a second witness — the two sections state one rule twice, which is the pattern the machine records as a standing-verdict, not a duplicate]
Bereshit Rabbah 93:12

F — INK ROW: "he fell on his brother Benjamin's NECK ‹צַוְּארֵי› ("tzavarei")" is written PLURAL — did Benjamin have two necks? — read as the TWO TEMPLES destined for Benjamin's portion and destined to be destroyed, with Benjamin weeping in return over the Tabernacle at Shiloh in Joseph's portion [the embrace read as a prophecy of two sanctuaries, priced at one letter]; and the closing rule: as Joseph was reconciled to his brothers only through weeping, so Israel will be redeemed only through weeping (Jeremiah 31:9)
Bereshit Rabbah 94:2

F — Pharaoh's provision read as split beans that soothe the uneasy soul; the LAW OF VOWS on OUR 45:23's three-word list — R. Yoshiya: in vows one follows COLLOQUIAL SPEECH, so grain is grain, bread is bread in its plain sense, and Rav Aḥa bar Eila derives from "food ‹מָזוֹן› ("mazon")" here that ALL foodstuffs are called food — against R. Yoḥanan's own usage, who having eaten boiled grain would say "I have not eaten food today" [a vow-interpretation rule grounded on this verse's inventory — testing-shelf candidate]; and "do not be agitated on the way" (45:24) opened three ways — do not take long strides, do not break off from Torah study, and enter the city while the sun still shines [travel conduct rules read off one clause]
Bereshit Rabbah 94:3

F — the liar's plight stated as a rule: even when he speaks the truth he is not believed — R. Ḥiyya's reading of "his heart went numb, for HE DID NOT BELIEVE THEM" (OUR 45:26), the brothers now paying for the bloodied tunic of gen_60; THE WAGONS ‹עֲגָלוֹת› ("agalot") read twice — the wagons Pharaoh sent carried ENGRAVED IDOLS and Judah burned them ("that tribe is experienced in burning idols"), and R. Levi's cipher: the wagons are the sign, because the last passage Jacob and Joseph studied together was the BEHEADED HEIFER ‹עֶגְלָה› ("egla") [the father-son password — a recognition token built on a pun, and the passage names it as what revived his spirit]; and "ENOUGH ‹רַב› ("rav")" at 45:28 read as GREAT — the greatness of my son, who kept his righteousness through more troubles than I bore

HEADLINES: the disclosure read as a JUDGMENT-DAY A-FORTIORI, stated twice by two authorities — if the youngest brother's rebuke left them unable to answer, how much more the rebuke of the Judge who is also litigant and bench; the identity proved by the BODY (he showed them the circumcision) and by the TONGUE ("my mouth speaks to you" = in the holy language, which the translation states as "in your language"); the plural "NECKS" read as the two Temples destined for Benjamin's portion and destined to fall; a VOW-INTERPRETATION rule that follows colloquial speech, taken from the three-word provision list, with R. Yoḥanan's own counter-usage; the liar's plight ("even when he speaks truth he is not believed") charged to the brothers of the bloodied tunic; and the BEHEADED-HEIFER PASSWORD — the wagons as the father-son recognition token built on a pun. Onkelos: the revived spirit named as THE SPIRIT OF PROPHECY, closing gen_64's claim that it had departed the day Joseph was taken. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

mat: Bereshit Rabbah 94:6

F — the night vision parsed: "I will go down with you and I will ALSO BRING YOU UP" (OUR 46:4) read as "you AND ALL THE RIGHTEOUS LIKE YOU" [the promise widened past the individual — the resurrection reading the block's ops must carry]; "Joseph will place his hand on your eyes" read two ways, as Joseph providing for all his needs and as Joseph closing his eyes in death; and A COUNTING RULE from OUR 46:7's roster (R. Yehuda bar Ilai): SONS' DAUGHTERS COUNT LIKE SONS, DAUGHTERS' SONS DO NOT [a lineage rule read off the list's own phrasing, and the rule the next row's arithmetic runs on]
Bereshit Rabbah 94:9

F — THE SEVENTY THAT COUNT SIXTY-NINE, the sweep's largest numeric row (opened, never credited): "have you ever seen a man given sixty-six cups and then three more, and count them as seventy?" — the missing member disputed FIVE ways: (a) YOKHEVED, conceived in Canaan and born "at the gates of Egypt," proven from Numbers 26:59's "who was born to Levi IN EGYPT," with the general principle that the Holy One counts this tribe from the womb (the Yedutun roster of five-called-six as its parallel case, and "one-quarter of Israel" read to the conjugal act); (b) JACOB himself, with the two-legions parable — the emperor completes whichever legion he stands with; (c) THE HOLY ONE, who went down with them; (d) ḤUSHIM SON OF DAN, counted double from the plural "the SONS of Dan" for one son — AND THE INK VARIANT RECORDED: in R. Meir's own Torah scroll they found it written "the SON of Dan," singular [a manuscript reading preserved inside the midrash — the class the credit guards forbid crediting unopened]; (e) SERAḤ DAUGHTER OF ASHER, self-identified in II Samuel 20:19's "I am the peaceful and faithful of Israel" — "I am the one who COMPLETED the tally of Israel in Egypt, and who delivered the faithful to the faithful, Joseph to Moses." Carried with it the wise woman's whole sugya at Abel: the siege law that a group must NOT deliver one soul of Israel even on pain of all being killed, UNLESS he was singled out by name as Sheva son of Bikhri was — with R. Yehuda's inside/outside distinction, R. Shimon's rule that one who revolts against the house of David is liable to death, and the two cases that test it (R. Yehoshua ben Levi handing over Ulla ben Kishar, after which Elijah stopped visiting him — "is that a mishnah of the pious?"; and the Sanhedrin handing over Yehoyakim to Nebuchadnezzar on the precedent of Sheva) [a capital law, its exception, and its two applications, all hanging off this block's count — the testing shelf's richest catch in Genesis]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:5

F — [anchored at OUR 46:4's "I will surely bring you up"; home verses Genesis 50:5-9, gen_73's span] the burial plot audited at the ink: "in my grave that I DUG ‹כָּרִיתִי› ("kariti") for myself" is not "that I ACQUIRED ‹לָקַחְתִּי›" — so it is read as "I HEAPED UP ‹הִכַּרְתִּי› money for it," recording the deal with Esau at Isaac's estate: Esau took the cash and left the burial plot, at a price [the Machpelah right bought twice, and gen_39's purchase is the first payment]; and the funeral procession read as a war footing — "up to this point for lament, from here on for battle," the doubled particle "BOTH chariots AND horsemen" (50:9) taken as an inclusion
Bereshit Rabbah 96:5

F — [anchored here; home verses Genesis 47:29-31, gen_70's span, back-credited there] WHY NOT BURIED IN EGYPT, four reasons on the record: the land's dust was destined to become lice; lest they make him an object of worship — with the rule that PUNISHMENT IS EXACTED FROM THE WORSHIPPED AS FROM THE WORSHIPPER (Exodus 12:12, with Daniel refusing Nebuchadnezzar's offering and Hiram's fate as the two test cases); lest Egypt earn merit through him; and the land-of-Israel doctrine — the dead of the Land rise first, one who dies abroad and is buried abroad dies twice (Jeremiah 20:6), and for the righteous buried abroad the Holy One bores TUNNELS through the earth and they roll to the Land where the spirit is restored (Ezekiel 37:12-14) [the burial-place claim that governs the last two blocks]; with "kindness and TRUTH" read as the kindness done to the dead, who cannot repay
kept: terse — R. Meir's exchange with the Samaritan over descent from Joseph, hung on Issachar's roster names at OUR 46:13; a polemic on lineage claims, no ops

HEADLINES: THE SEVENTY THAT COUNT SIXTY-NINE — the missing member disputed five ways (Yokheved born at the gates of Egypt; Jacob himself, with the two-legions parable; the Holy One who went down with them; Ḥushim son of Dan counted double, WITH R. MEIR'S OWN SCROLL READING "the SON of Dan" singular; and Seraḥ daughter of Asher, self-identified centuries later as the one who completed the tally); the SIEGE LAW carried with it — a group may not deliver one soul of Israel even on pain of all dying, unless he was singled out by name, with its inside/outside distinction and two hard applications; the lineage counting rule (sons' daughters count, daughters' sons do not); the promise "I will bring you up" widened to all the righteous; and the burial doctrine that governs the last blocks — the worshipped punished as the worshipper, and the tunnels through which the righteous buried abroad roll to the Land. mat: Bereshit Rabbah 95:4

F — WHY FIVE, AND WHICH FIVE: "from the EDGE ‹מִקְצֵה› ("miktze") of his brothers he took five men" (OUR 47:2) read as the ones at the margin — THE WEAK ONES — named as Reuben, Levi, Benjamin, Simeon and Issachar, because Joseph reasoned that if Pharaoh saw the strong he would conscript them as his warriors [a deliberate concealment of military capacity — an administrative op with a motive]; and THE TEST FOR WHO WAS STRONG, read backwards out of Moses' blessing: whoever's name is REPEATED there was mighty — Judah, Naphtali, Asher, Dan, Zebulun, Gad, each cited (Deuteronomy 33:7, 23, 24, 22, 18, 20) — and those six are exactly the ones withheld from the audience [a census built by a spelling test in a later book, deciding a roster in this one]; with Joseph's retort to the Egyptians who claimed to have nothing — "your horse is before me; you are exposed like a peeled onion"
Bereshit Rabbah 96:1

F — THE SCRIBAL LAYOUT READ AS MEANING: why is this portion CLOSED ‹סְתוּמָה› ("setuma") — the only weekly portion with no open space before it — three answers: because with Jacob's death the ENSLAVEMENT BEGAN and their eyes were closed; because Jacob sought to reveal THE END OF DAYS and it was SEALED ‹נִסְתַּם› from him; and because he was shielded from all the world's troubles in those years [a claim about the physical layout of the scroll itself, in the class the credit guards require opening — the manuscript's white space carrying three readings]
Bereshit Rabbah 96:3

F — "the time for ISRAEL to die APPROACHED" (OUR 47:29) read against Ecclesiastes 8:8 ("no man rules the spirit… and there is no dominion on the day of death"), with a THREE-CASE CENSUS of authority ebbing at the end: Moses' own trumpets sequestered so another could not sound them, so he had to summon the elders by word (Deuteronomy 31:28); Pinḥas acting before Moses at Shittim; and David demoted in the ink itself — "the time for DAVID to die approached" (I Kings 2:1), not "for KING David" [the title dropped as the dominion goes]; so too Jacob here lowers himself before his son — "if I have found favor in your eyes" [the machine's state change: the patriarch petitioning his own child]
Bereshit Rabbah 96:4

F — Reish Lakish on the same verb: "you shall LIE DOWN but you shall not die" — and the "APPROACHED ‹וַיִּקְרְבוּ›" heard as a CLAIM FILED, the day itself complaining that it cannot end while he lives; then the arithmetic rule, opened as a numeric claim: WHOEVER HAS "APPROACHED" WRITTEN OF HIM DID NOT REACH HIS FATHERS' YEARS — David seventy against Boaz, Oved and Yishai; Moses one hundred twenty against Amram's one hundred thirty-seven; and Jacob's ONE HUNDRED FORTY-SEVEN against Abraham's one hundred seventy-five and Isaac's one hundred eighty, which is OUR 47:28's own number [the verse's count is the rule's proof, and the rule explains the verb the block opens its death sequence with]

teach.en: The declared spine read end to end; the unit spans the whole chapter, so the reading crosses the Vayechi seam at 47:28. HEADLINES: WHY FIVE BROTHERS AND WHICH — the weak ones presented so Pharaoh would not conscript the strong, with the strength-census built by a spelling test in Moses' blessing (whoever's name is repeated there was mighty); THE CLOSED PORTION — the scroll's own missing white space read three ways (the enslavement beginning, the End sealed from him, the shielding from troubles); the dominion-ebbs census, with David's royal title dropped from the ink as his day approaches; and the rule that "APPROACHED" is written of whoever fell short of his fathers' years — proven by this unit's own 147 against 175 and 180. Onkelos: the resettlement read as transfer FROM CITY TO CITY, the bow at the head of the BED left as a bed, and the fifth kept as a standing statute with the priests' land exempt — the block's one permanent legislative act. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

mat: Bereshit Rabbah 97:1

F — the tribes' SUSPICION recorded: when Joseph came out from the blessing with his face glowing, the brothers said "everyone attaches himself to the successful one — he blesses him because he is king," and Jacob answered with "FEAR THE LORD, HIS HOLY ONES, for those who fear Him lack nothing" (Psalms 34:10) [the blessing challenged as favouritism at the moment it is given — the same suspicion the tunic drew in gen_60, now aimed at the deathbed; carried as the brothers' recorded state]
Bereshit Rabbah 97:2

F — WHAT "WALKED BEFORE HIM" MEANS, a two-way dispute on OUR 48:15: R. Yoḥanan reads a SHEPHERD standing and watching his flock walk before him — so the walking is for our sake, and "we need His glory"; Reish Lakish reads a KING walking with the ELDERS BEFORE HIM in procession — so the walking is honor paid, and "He needs our glory" [the direction of dependence argued off one preposition; and see O2 below, where the translation votes with Reish Lakish by rendering the verb SERVED]
Bereshit Rabbah 97:5

F — EPHRAIM FIRST EVERYWHERE, a nine-item precedence census built from OUR 48:20's "he set Ephraim before Manasseh": in genealogies, in the census lineage (Numbers 1:32-35), in inheritance (Joshua 16-17), in the banners (Numbers 2:18-20), in the princes' offerings (the seventh day before the eighth, Numbers 7:48), in judges (Joshua before Gideon), in kings (Jeroboam before Jehu), and in the blessing formula itself [the crossing of the hands verified as a standing precedence across four later books — the strongest form of the pattern the machine records, a claim the text keeps paying out]

teach.tr: nikra kulo (read in full — the declared spine)
teach.en: The declared spine read end to end — THE HIGHEST CREDIT RATIO OF THE WALK, thirteen standing credits against three fresh sections: this block's substance was read at its narrative seats chapters earlier and arrives already verdicted. HEADLINES: EPHRAIM FIRST EVERYWHERE — a nine-item precedence census (genealogies, census lineage, inheritance, banners, princes' offerings, judges, kings, and the blessing formula itself) verifying the crossed hands across four later books; the two-way dispute on what "walked BEFORE Him" means — a shepherd watching his flock (we need His glory) against a king with elders walking before him (He needs our glory); and the brothers' recorded SUSPICION that the blessing was favouritism to the successful son. Onkelos: the sword and bow of the last verse rendered MY PRAYER AND MY PLEA — the patriarch disarmed, while the chain independently rules the sword was Esau's all along; the crossing of the hands declared DELIBERATE in the text; the walking rendered SERVED, voting with one side of the block's own dispute; and the Word-as-support formula at its third seat. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

mat: Bereshit Rabbah 98:2

F — THE END REVEALED AND SEALED, the chapter's governing claim: "I will tell you what will BEFALL YOU AT THE END OF DAYS" (OUR 49:1) — R. Simon says he showed them Gog's downfall, R. Yehuda the building of the Temple, and the Rabbis say HE CAME TO REVEAL THE END AND IT WAS CONCEALED FROM HIM, proven by the fact that the next word out of his mouth is "Reuben" [the machine's reason the chapter is a blessing and not a prophecy of dates]; only TWO people had the End revealed then concealed — Jacob and Daniel (Daniel 12:4); with the parable of the king's confidant who looked up, saw the king's face, and told his sons only "be careful of the king's honor"; and "GATHER… ASSEMBLE" opened four ways — gather from Egypt to Rameses, gather the ten tribes to Judah and Benjamin, PURIFY yourselves, and the Rabbis' reading as a command against dissension ("you shall all be one assembly"), sealed with the written form of Ezekiel 37:16, where "his COMPANIONS" is written as "his COMPANION," singular — Israel made one group [an ink claim carrying a unity ruling]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:3

F — **THE SHEMA'S ORIGIN AT THIS DEATHBED**: "listen to ‹אֵל› Israel your father" (OUR 49:2) parsed two ways — "listen to the GOD ‹אֵל› of Israel your father" (R. Yudan), and "your father Israel is LIKE a god" (R. Pinḥas: as the Holy One creates and distributes worlds, so your father). Then Elazar ben Aḥui's derivation: Jacob asked his twelve sons whether any dissent was in their hearts, and they answered "HEAR, ISRAEL" — addressing their father — "THE LORD IS OUR GOD, THE LORD IS ONE" (Deuteronomy 6:4), and he replied with his lips "BLESSED BE THE NAME OF HIS GLORIOUS KINGDOM FOREVER" — which is why Israel recites it morning and evening, addressing the patriarch in the cave of Machpelah: "the matter you commanded us, we still practice" [the daily liturgy's second line, the one recited in an undertone, sourced to this block's own verse — the strongest liturgical claim in the Genesis walk]; and the third-person phrasing of 49:2 read as an ANGEL doing the assembling, or the Divine Spirit (R. Tanḥuma)
Bereshit Rabbah 98:5

F — the Simeon-and-Levi rebuke, four findings: "they are BROTHERS" — brothers of Dina, not brothers of Joseph [the selective fraternity indicted]; "weapons of villainy are their ‹מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם›" read as the weapons being STOLEN GOODS fit only for Esau, who SOLD ‹מָכַר› the birthright; "in their anger they killed A MAN ‹אִישׁ›" (singular) identified as Hamor, and "they HAMSTRUNG ‹עִקְּרוּ› an OX ‹שׁוֹר›" re-read as "they UNDERMINED ‹עָקְרוּ› the WALL ‹שׁוּר› of the proselytes" — the massacre after the circumcision made every future convert fear the same [a claim about damage to an institution, not to persons]; **AND THE PTOLEMY EMENDATION RECORDED**: this is named as one of the places the elders altered for King Ptolemy, writing "killed an ox… undermined a trough" so the king would not read them as murderers [the two-shelves seam at its sharpest — the chain preserving a rival translation's deliberate change, beside our Onkelos, on one verse]; with the curse aimed at the ANGER and not the men (the king cursing the serpent that would bite his son), and the dispersal fulfilled — Levi given no portion but "I am your portion," Simeon's poor scattered as scribes and his cities given to the Levites
Bereshit Rabbah 98:7

F — Judah the lion cub: "FROM THE PREY ‹מִטֶּרֶף› you rose, my son" read as from the prey of JOSEPH and the prey of TAMAR — the two capital cases Judah stopped [the kingship earned by the two interventions gen_60 and gen_61 recorded]; and the two crouching verbs timed to dynastic history — "he crouched ‹רָבַץ›" from Peretz to David and "lay ‹שָׁכַב›" from David to Zedekiah, or from Peretz to Zedekiah and then to the messianic king; also read as this world and the World to Come, and as times with enemies and without
Bereshit Rabbah 98:8

F — "THE SCEPTER SHALL NOT DEPART FROM JUDAH" (OUR 49:10) read institutionally: the SCEPTER ‹שֵׁבֶט› is the Sanhedrin that flogs and subjugates, the "lawgiver from between his feet" the two scribes of the judges standing right and left, "until Shiloh comes" the messianic king, and "to him nations will ‹יִקְּהַת›" read as he will BLUNT ‹יַקְהֶה› the teeth of the nations; and **A DOCUMENTARY CLAIM**: a GENEALOGICAL SCROLL WAS FOUND IN JERUSALEM tracing Hillel to David, R. Ḥiyya the Great to Shefatya son of Avital, and eight other houses to named ancestors [a physical document cited as evidence for a standing rule — the class the credit guards require opening]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:9

F — the vine and the foal (OUR 49:11) read agriculturally (even a poor vine needs a donkey to carry its yield; the "wine" white and the "blood of grapes" red) and messianically (R. Neḥemya: the vine brought into His city; the Rabbis: bound to the vine, and the donkey-rider of Zechariah 9:9); with a recorded dispute on WHAT THE MESSIAH COMES TO DO — R. Ḥanin holds Israel will not need his teaching at all (Isaiah 11:10, "the NATIONS will seek him — not Israel"), so he comes only to gather the exiles and give THIRTY commandments, against Rav, who reads the thirty as thirty MIGHTY MEN [the disagreement carried as recorded, both readings of Zechariah 11:12's thirty]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:10

F — "his eyes RED from wine, his teeth WHITE from milk" (OUR 49:12) read as the Sanhedrin: MOST OF THE SANHEDRIN CAME FROM JUDAH, who sit arranging Torah with their teeth until they express it clear as milk [the tribal blessing read as a judicial census]; with the southern-scholars reading and the wine-and-age proverb
Bereshit Rabbah 98:11

F — Zebulun at the shore (OUR 49:13) and the JONAH'S-TRIBE DISPUTE settled by the verse: R. Levi proved Jonah from Zebulun (Gat Ḥefer in Zebulun's lot, Joshua 19:13 with II Kings 14:25), R. Yoḥanan proved him from Asher (Tzarefat of Sidon, I Kings 17:9) — and the resolution reads OUR OWN CLAUSE: "his ‹יַרְכָתוֹ› shall be upon Sidon" — the THIGH ‹יָרֵךְ› from which he came was of Sidon, so his father was of Zebulun and his mother of Asher [a prophet's parentage decided by one word of this blessing]; with the story of R. Levi buying the Sabbath turn for two sela and being told "you spoke consolation standing; you will speak it sitting" — he served as preacher twenty-two years
Bereshit Rabbah 98:12

F — Issachar the strong-boned donkey (OUR 49:14-15) read as learning made conspicuous, the "sheepfolds" as the THREE ROWS OF SCHOLARS seated before the court, "he saw REST that it was good" as the Torah, and "he became a tribute-servant" as the TWO HUNDRED HEADS OF SANHEDRIN who came from Issachar [the tribe as the judiciary's supply]; with a full geographic alternative (the donkey's shape as the valleys and Mount Tabor between them), the dispute over whether Issachar left Canaanite remnants, and the converts drawn by the tribe's produce and its scholars
Bereshit Rabbah 98:13

F — Dan avenging his people "as ONE ‹כְּאַחַד› of the tribes" (OUR 49:16) read as "like the MOST DISTINGUISHED ‹כַּמְיֻחָד› of the tribes," i.e. Judah — with R. Yehoshua bar Neḥemya's rider that had it not cleaved to Judah it would not have produced even its one judge; and "like the UNIQUE ONE ‹כִּיחִידוֹ› of the world," who needs no help, so Samson needed none: the fresh jawbone read as three days old (or from a twin-bearing donkey — "a donkey, two donkeys," Judges 15:16), the thirst of one who prattles, and the spring opened BETWEEN HIS TEETH by the merit of Moses' blessing "leaps FROM Bashan" read as "from between his teeth"
Bereshit Rabbah 98:14

F — Dan the serpent (OUR 49:17) mapped clause by clause onto Samson: found among women as the serpent was with Eve; restrained by oath as the serpent by charm (Judges 15:12); all his strength in his head, as the hair (Judges 16:17); and his venom killing after death — "the dead he killed in his death were more than in his life"; then "his rider FALLS BACKWARD" read as Jacob's own petition that the collapsing temple fall backward so the family could recover the body from the rubble; and OUR 49:18's cry — "FOR YOUR SALVATION I HOPE, LORD" — explained as Jacob seeing Samson, believing him the messianic king, then seeing that he would die: "will this one also die?" [the verse that interrupts the blessings given a reason]; with R. Yitzḥak's census that EVERYTHING comes through hope — suffering, sanctification of the Name, the merit of the fathers, the World to Come, grace and forgiveness, each with its verse
Bereshit Rabbah 98:19

F — "they EMBITTERED him and SHOT at him" (OUR 49:23) counted three ways — a son who embittered his brothers, a son whose brothers embittered him, a son who embittered his master's wife — and the verse settles which was worst by the word "they SHOT" [the blame apportioned by a verb]; then the ARROW TEACHING: why liken slanderers to arrows rather than any other weapon — because every other weapon strikes near and this strikes far, "so evil speech spoken in Rome kills in Syria"; and the broom-bush coals (Psalms 120:4) — all coals die from within, these burn on inside though quenched without, "so one who receives evil speech: even if you appease him and he is appeased, it still burns within" — with the case of a broom fire that burned twelve months [the sweep's fullest statement of the slander model that gen_60 opened with the three reports]
Bereshit Rabbah 99:1

F — THE TEMPLE'S SITE ARGUED FROM THIS CHAPTER: R. Yosei HaGelili reads Psalms 68:17's contending mountains literally (Tabor and Carmel racing to host the giving of the Torah, told "you are all HUMPED ‹גַּבְנֻנִּים› — idolatry was done on your peaks," and Sinai chosen for being clean); R. Akiva reads it of THE TRIBES contending over where the Temple would stand, told "you are all righteous, but you are all ‹גַּבְנֻנִּים› — THIEVES: every one of you took part in the sale of Joseph. But Benjamin, who did not, is 'the mountain God desired'" [the sale of gen_60 disqualifying eleven tribes from the sanctuary, and Benjamin's absence from that crime becoming the site's title — the strongest single consequence the sale has drawn in the whole walk]; with R. Yehuda's counter (the portion of Judah) and R. Shimon's (the portion of the one who died at Ephrath, read to Benjamin via "the beast of the forest" — OUR 49:27's wolf)
Bereshit Rabbah 99:3

F — Benjamin the ravening wolf (OUR 49:27) read FOUR ways, each with morning and evening assigned: his JUDGES (Ehud snatching Eglon's heart, with the vestibule read as the ordered angels), his KINGDOM (Saul seizing the kingship, "in the morning" his wars and "in the evening" his trespass; and Esther seizing the crown, "in the morning" Haman's house given her, "in the evening" Mordekhai set over it), his LAND (Jericho ripening first, Beth El last), and R. Pinḥas's reading — THE ALTAR, which snatches the offerings: the morning lamb and the twilight lamb (Numbers 28:4) [the daily offering schedule read out of a tribal blessing]
Bereshit Rabbah 99:4

F — the summary verse (OUR 49:28) pressed: it already says "he blessed them," so why "EACH MAN ACCORDING TO HIS BLESSING he blessed them"? Because after comparing Judah to a lion, Dan to a serpent, Naphtali to a doe and Benjamin to a wolf, HE THEN INCLUDED THEM ALL IN ONE ANOTHER'S BLESSINGS and made them all lions and all serpents — proof: Dan called a serpent here and a lion cub in Deuteronomy 33:22 [the blessings distributed and then pooled — a rule about how the whole set applies, ending in "you are all fair, my love, there is no blemish in you"]
Bereshit Rabbah 99:9

F — WHY ZEBULUN PRECEDES ISSACHAR though born later (OUR 49:13 before 49:14): because Zebulun traded and Issachar studied, and Zebulun came and FED HIM — so precedence went to the supporter, "it is a tree of life TO THOSE WHO UPHOLD IT" (Proverbs 3:18); with Moses' matching pair, "rejoice Zebulun in your going out, and Issachar in your tents" — the tents are yours because you enable him to sit in them [the support-partnership rule read off the blessing order, one of the tradition's standing institutions, sourced here]
Bereshit Rabbah 99:11

F — the second Dan reading, and a REDIRECTION: the serpent goes alone where all beasts go in pairs, and Samson was vindictive as a serpent ("let me avenge one vengeance," Judges 16:28) — but when Jacob saw him he said "FOR YOUR SALVATION I HOPE," because THIS one will not bring salvation; it will come from GAD — "he will raid at their HEEL ‹עָקֵב›" (OUR 49:19) read to the one who comes AT THE END ‹בְּעָקֵב›, Elijah the prophet (Malachi 3:23), held to be of Gad [the messianic expectation moved off Dan onto Gad by one word — dual-track with row 11, which leaves it on Samson]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:16

F — terse: Asher's "rich bread" (OUR 49:20) read three ways at once from one feminine adjective — his LAND is rich, his BREAD is rich, and he produces wearers of the EIGHT ‹שְׁמוֹנָה› garments, the high priests [a pun carrying a priestly-lineage claim]; with "royal delicacies" as fine pastries and the oil of unripe olives
Bereshit Rabbah 98:17

F — Naphtali the doe LET LOOSE (OUR 49:21) read of his land as irrigated fields, with the Kinneret place-name dispute; then of Deborah SENDING for Barak from Kedesh Naphtali (Judges 4:6-7) and the song that followed; and the closing item that reaches into the next block: when they went up to bury Jacob and the Hittites contested the grave, NAPHTALI RAN LIKE A DOE TO EGYPT AND BROUGHT THE DEED [the burial-dispute exhibit, whose scene is gen_73's]
Bereshit Rabbah 98:1

F — terse: the chapter framed by Psalms 57:3 — "I call to God Most High" on the New Year, "to the God who COMPLETES for me" on the Day of Atonement (the two goats' lots) — and applied to Jacob: the Holy One AGREED WITH HIM to give each son as befitted him [the blessings ratified from above, which is what makes them binding rather than paternal wishes]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:1

F — INK ROW: Psalms 100:3's "‹וְלֹא› ("velo")" is written with one letter and read as another — R. Yehuda bar Simon builds on the WRITTEN form ("He made us and NOT we ourselves," against Pharaoh's "my river is mine and I made myself"), R. Aḥa on the READ form ("He made us and TO HIM we belong") [the written-and-read pair carried both ways, the class never credited unopened]; with OUR 49:33's "Jacob FINISHED commanding his sons" counted as one of three command-verses (49:29, 49:33, 50:12)
Bereshit Rabbah 100:2

F — THE THREE COMMANDS itemized: against idolatry, against blaspheming the Name, and the BEARING OF THE BIER — "let no uncircumcised man touch my bier, lest the Divine Presence depart; carry me THREE FROM THE NORTH, THREE FROM THE SOUTH, THREE FROM THE EAST, THREE FROM THE WEST — and just as you do for me, so you will be arrayed in four banners in the wilderness with the Presence in the centre" [the wilderness camp's formation prefigured by a funeral order — a standing arrangement claimed to originate at this deathbed]; carried with the deathbed-instruction parallels (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's three, with the widow's residence rule and its reasoning; R. Ḥizkiya's two more; and the burial-garment customs of R. Yoḥanan, R. Yoshiya and R. Yirmeya, the last asking for staff and sandals "so that if I am summoned I may rise ready")

teach.tr: nikra kulo (read in full — the declared spine)
teach.en: The declared spine read end to end — THE DENSEST BLOCK OF THE GENESIS WALK (6,024 enumerated, 82 declared, 82 outside-scope primaries, and the only block where every fresh section came back material). HEADLINES: THE SHEMA SOURCED TO THIS DEATHBED — the sons answering "Hear, Israel" to their father and Jacob replying with the line said in an undertone ever since; THE END REVEALED AND SEALED, with Jacob and Daniel the only two it happened to; THE TEMPLE'S SITE decided by who did NOT join the sale of Joseph — eleven tribes disqualified, Benjamin's portion chosen; the scepter read as the Sanhedrin, with a genealogical scroll found in Jerusalem as evidence; the four-banner wilderness formation prefigured by the bier order; the Zebulun-Issachar support partnership; the arrow-and-broom-coals model of slander (evil speech spoken in Rome kills in Syria); and the Ptolemy emendation recorded beside our own translation — three layers on one verse. ONKELOS CHANGES GENRE HERE: through forty-eight chapters a translation, in this chapter an interpretive paraphrase — the Messiah named at Shiloh, Reuben's three forfeited portions written into the verse, Benjamin's portion given the Temple outright, and seven consecutive blessings rendered as their fulfilments. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

mat: Bereshit Rabbah 100:4

F — INK ROW at OUR 50:4: "the days of his weeping PASSED ‹וַיַּעַבְרוּ›" against Moses' "the days of weeping CONCLUDED ‹וַיִּתְּמוּ›" (Deuteronomy 34:8) — the difference read as company: Moses had no others weeping so his mourning simply ended, but Jacob had others weeping [the verb chosen by who else is in the room]; and a rule of court conduct — Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's HOUSEHOLD rather than to Pharaoh, routing the request through the nursemaid to the queen to the king, BECAUSE A MOURNER MAY NOT ENTER THE KING'S PALACE [the reason the verse's odd indirection exists, stated as a standing rule]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:6

F — the threshing floor of ‹אָטָד› ("Atad," bramble) at OUR 50:10-11: R. Shmuel bar Naḥman reports searching the entire Scripture and finding no place of that name — is there a threshing floor for a bramble? — so these were the CANAANITES, fit to be trampled like brambles, and the question becomes why they were spared: because of the KINDNESS they showed at Jacob's bier, disputed four ways (they untied their belts, or the ties of their packs, or merely POINTED WITH A FINGER and said "this is a heavy mourning for Egypt," or straightened up in respect); with the a-fortiori — if these, who moved neither hand nor foot but only pointed, were delivered, then Israel who perform kindness with hand and foot, all the more so; and R. Abahu's accounting: THE SEVENTY DAYS between Haman's two letters correspond to the seventy days Egypt mourned Jacob [a merit ledger kept across a thousand years, paid out at Esther's crisis]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:8

F — WHY THE BROTHERS FEARED (OUR 50:15), two suspicions and one defence, twice: R. Levi says because Joseph no longer invited them to his table, and R. Yitzḥak says because he went and LOOKED INTO THE PIT — and to both R. Tanḥuma answers that his intention was for Heaven (he would not sit above Judah the king and Reuben the firstborn now that his father was gone; he went to bless God for the deliverance at the pit's mouth), "but that is not what they said — they said 'perhaps Joseph will hate us'" [the machine's cleanest case of an innocent act read as a threat, with both readings kept]; and **THE PEACE RULING**: R. Shimon ben Gamliel — GREAT IS PEACE, for even the tribes SPOKE WORDS THAT WERE NOT SO in order to make peace between themselves and Joseph, since "your father commanded before his death" (50:16) records a command WE NEVER FIND HIM GIVING [an untruth licensed by name in the text's own record — a testing-shelf ruling of the first order]; with Joseph's answer read as grief: "is this how my brothers suspect me?"
Bereshit Rabbah 100:9

F — "he SPOKE TO THEIR HEART" (OUR 50:21) — can a person speak to a heart? — read as words that settle the heart, and the consolation itemized: you were likened to the DUST of the earth, the BEASTS of the field, and the STARS — can anyone eliminate these? ten stars could not overcome one; shall I change the world's order and eliminate twelve tribes, who answer to the twelve hours and the twelve constellations? [the promise argued from cosmology]; then R. Simlai's four-part self-interest argument in Joseph's mouth — you are the body and I the head, and what use is a head without a body; before you came they called me a slave, and through you I proved my lineage; if I killed you they would say he kept no faith with his brothers, so with whom would he keep faith; or they would say these were never his brothers at all, for in the end he contrived a pretext and killed them; and shall I be an antagonist to my father, who begets while I bury, or to the Holy One, who blesses while I diminish? — closing with the a-fortiori: if Joseph consoled the tribes so, how much more when the Holy One comes to console Jerusalem (Isaiah 40:1)
Bereshit Rabbah 100:11

F — THE OATH AND ITS TIMING at OUR 50:25: one might have thought the bones were to be carried up at once — the verse "you shall carry my bones up from here WITH YOU" (Exodus 13:19) fixes it to the exodus, WHEN YOU GO UP; and from that same word "with you" it is derived that THEY CARRIED UP THE BONES OF ALL THE TRIBES [a law of scope read from one preposition, and the hinge on which this book hands off to the next]; with the embalming disputed — R. Yehuda says the physicians, R. Pinḥas says THE TRIBES embalmed him, reading "they embalmed him" against "these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt" (Exodus 1:1) [the book's last act performed by the brothers who sold him]
Bereshit Rabbah 100:10

F — terse: the SIX PAIRS whose years were equal, with OUR 50:22's one hundred and ten placing Joseph beside JOSHUA — Rebecca and Kehat, Levi and Amram, Joseph and Joshua, Samuel and Solomon, Moses and Hillel the Elder, R. Yoḥanan ben Zakkai and R. Akiva; with the three-forty-year division of Moses' life and the same threefold division for R. Yoḥanan ben Zakkai and R. Akiva [a numeric census, opened; the pairing of Joseph with Joshua closes the arc gen_60's dream-as-deed row opened, where Joshua commanded the sun as "my father's purchase"]

teach.tr: nikra kulo (read in full — the declared spine)
teach.en: The declared spine read end to end. THE LAST BLOCK OF GENESIS — with this reading the book stands read through from 1:1 to 50:26 under the declared scope. HEADLINES: THE PEACE RULING — great is peace, for the tribes spoke words that were not so to make peace, the text itself recording a command from Jacob we never find him giving; the BONES-OATH SCOPE RULE — "with you" fixing both the timing (at the going up, not at once) and the extension to all the tribes' bones, the hinge on which this book hands off to the next; the mourner who may not enter the palace, explaining the verse's indirection; the Canaanites spared for a pointed finger, with the seventy mourning days credited back at Esther's seventy days between letters; the brothers' fear read from an uninvited meal and a look into the pit, with both innocent readings kept beside it; and the six equal-year pairs placing Joseph beside Joshua. Onkelos: "am I in the place of God?" reversed into "I AM ONE WHO FEARS GOD," and the scribal strength-token standing at the book's end. Findings in the ledger; dual-track; no machine ops changed.

teach.work: Targum Onkelos, Leviticus 13:2,3,8 — Tier-A translation read at derive time (FETCHLOG 2026-07-31)
teach.en: The translation renders tzara'at as SEGIRU/SEGIRUTA — 'the SHUTTING/confinement-disease': the condition named by its own quarantine procedure, on the root of ve-hisgir (and of Gen 2:21's flesh-closure and 7:16's ark-closure). The received Aramaic fuses what the machine tracks as two symbols (the disease noun; the confine verb) into one root — the strongest translation-level witness yet that the procedure IS the concept.

teach.work: Targum Onkelos, Leviticus 13:5 — Tier-A
teach.en: The [OPEN] idiom amad be-einav ('stood in its/his eyes') resolved by the translation to 'stood AS IT WAS' — the appearance reading, against the priest's-eyes reading. First resolution witness; the chain-primary discussion queued with Sifra/Negaim.

teach.work: Sifra Tazria (Parashat Nega'im) 1ff; Mishnah Negaim 1:1, 3:1; Bavli Shevuot 6a-b; Bavli Arakhin 15b-16b; Bereshit Rabbah 41:2 — the chapter's chain-primaries, NOT in the local cache; day's Tier-A triage queue
teach.en: Named, not yet read (observation tier): the Sifra parashah (the 13 middot's own home text) and tractate Negaim own this chapter; Shevuot 6a-b (the four shades) bears on Onkelos's amka ('deep-spot') for the raised se'et; Arakhin 15b-16b carries the tzara'at-and- speech-sin frame that would bear on the se'et/Cain join; BR 41:2 reads Gen 12:17's nega debut as tzara'at. THE TRIPWIRE TEST: when these enter the cache, the detector's absent legal devices (ein li ela 'I have only'; ribah/miet ha-katuv 'Scripture included/ excluded'; dibber ha-katuv ba-hoveh 'the usual case') are predicted to fire for the first time.
